oewn-00597527-v.learner: To have something fixed in your memory.
examples: She knows the whole poem by heart.
He knows Latin and Greek.

oewn-00598039-v.learner: To have felt or lived through a state, situation, feeling or sensation yourself.
examples: Few of them had ever known real hunger.

oewn-00609926-v.learner: To see, hear or notice something and find that it is familiar.
examples: I knew her voice the moment she spoke.

oewn-00610224-v.learner: To understand what someone or something is really like.
examples: We all knew him as a quiet and careful man.

oewn-00610056-v.learner: To be able to tell things apart and see that they are different.
examples: He doesn't know a rose from a tulip.

oewn-00594278-v.learner: To accept that someone is what they claim to be, or to accept their power and authority.
examples: The villagers would know no master but the old lord.
The old text says that Adam knew Eve.

oewn-00941001-s.learner: Not yet tried or tested by experience.
examples: They are young in the ways of the world

oewn-00821577-s.learner: Of crops: picked at an early stage, before they have fully matured.
examples: We ate young corn straight from the field.

oewn-06719443-n.learner: A prize you earn for taking part in a school sport.
examples: She earned a letter in basketball in her second year.

oewn-10274904-n.learner: An owner who lets another person use something, usually a house or rooms, for payment.
examples: The letter of the rooms came to collect the rent every month.
He glanced away when she looked at him.

oewn-00237168-r.learner: So that something is removed or got rid of.
examples: The rotten boards had to be torn away.

oewn-00236800-r.learner: In or into the right place, especially so that something is stored or kept safe.
examples: Put your books away before dinner.
Her jewels were locked away in a safe.

oewn-00235026-r.learner: Out of your possession, so that you no longer have it.
examples: She gave away all her old clothes.

oewn-00236477-r.learner: Used to show that an action keeps going, without a break or at a steady pace.
examples: He worked away at his letters all afternoon.

oewn-00235782-r.learner: Out of the way, especially out of your thoughts.
examples: She pushed the worry away and went on reading.

oewn-00235417-r.learner: Kept back to be used later, not now.
examples: She kept a little money tucked away for later.

oewn-00237300-r.learner: Freely, or as much and whenever you want.
examples: Ask away, and I will answer anything.

oewn-00954873-v.learner: To give out information, so that it becomes known.
examples: The police hoped the driver would talk and tell them what he had seen.

oewn-00832422-v.learner: To give a lecture or a talk.
examples: She talked on modern poetry to a hall full of students.

oewn-10688105-n.learner: A person who is tested or watched in an experiment or other study; someone who is being investigated.
examples: Each subject in the study was asked to sleep for eight hours.

oewn-09648571-n.learner: A person who owes loyalty to a nation.
examples: He was born a British subject.

oewn-06320921-n.learner: In grammar, one of the two main parts of a sentence: the part that the rest of the sentence says something about.
examples: In the sentence 'The dog barked', the subject is 'the dog'.

oewn-04354303-n.learner: A person, object or scene that an artist or photographer chooses to show in a picture.
examples: The painter chose his own mother as the subject of the portrait.

oewn-06321115-n.learner: In logic, the first term of a proposition.
examples: In the proposition 'All men are mortal', the subject is 'men'.

oewn-00426024-v.learner: To begin to exist, or to arrive on the scene.
examples: Life first appeared on Earth billions of years ago.

oewn-00426920-v.learner: To be published or put out.
examples: Her first novel appeared in 1811.

oewn-02603759-v.learner: To come formally before an authority, such as a court.
examples: He must appear before the judge on Monday.

oewn-01725046-v.learner: To play a character on stage, or to take part in a play or a similar show.
examples: She appeared as Juliet in the school play.

oewn-00664507-v.learner: To take care to do something, or to make certain of something.
examples: The guard walked round the house to assure that every window was shut.

oewn-00885532-v.learner: To make a promise, or to commit yourself to something.
examples: He assured her that he would come back for her before winter.

oewn-01435927-v.learner: To go after something or someone and bring or take them back.
examples: The dog ran off to bring back the stick.

oewn-01436773-v.learner: To have someone or something come along with you.
examples: Can I bring my cousin to the dinner?

oewn-00135665-v.learner: To put someone or something into a different state.
examples: His gambling brought him into debt.

oewn-00769379-v.learner: To cause or persuade someone to do something.
examples: Nothing could bring her to speak of it again.

oewn-02329474-v.learner: To give a quality to something.
examples: She brought great skill to the role.

oewn-02252172-v.learner: To be sold for a certain price.
examples: The old house brought a good price.

oewn-01621566-v.learner: To put something forward in a court of law.
examples: They decided to bring a case against the company.

oewn-01812185-v.learner: To catch the attention of someone.
examples: The cries brought the neighbours running.

oewn-02475618-n.learner: All the people living on the earth.
examples: Half the world now lives in cities.

oewn-05817904-n.learner: Everything you have lived through, which shapes how things seem to you.
examples: When his father died, his whole world fell apart.

oewn-09503939-n.learner: A part of the earth that can be thought about on its own.
examples: The underwater world is full of strange fish.

oewn-05678816-n.learner: The matters of life on earth, as opposed to heaven and life after death.
examples: She left the world behind and entered a convent.
